story.iWant: an external reference price with seeded shocks and an oracle that lags it by heartbeat and deviation rules
story.soThat: oracle delay is a first-class, calibratable parameter
story.tasks: - Carry-over: split AMM cumulative fees by token (AC: 1) - Reference price process (AC: 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 12) - Oracle (AC: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) - Integration (AC: 11) - Tests, lint, close out (AC: 13)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: See story file ACs 1–13. The price-process and oracle-rule blocks in Dev Notes are normative.

docs.doc: Normative update rules, rng-draw guard, reason strings, registration order.
Fee-split ruling; construction-vs-execution rule; PegView ownership.

existing.reason: The only randomness source; numpy Generator.

dependencies.python: numpy (installed) for standard_normal; math.exp. No new dependencies.

story-context.constraints: - New files: src/depeg_sim/environment/price_process.py, src/depeg_sim/protocol/oracle.py, tests/test_price_process.py, tests/test_oracle.py, tests/test_oracle_integration.py. Task 1 touches amm.py and test_amm.py only. - ctx.rng.standard_normal() is the only random call; exactly one per step and only when volatility_per_step > 0. - Oracle holds a reference to the price source object; it does not look it up by name through the registry (keeps the dependency explicit and testable). - Oracle does NOT implement PegView. isinstance(oracle, PegView) must be False (test it). - Neither module is an ActionTarget. No execute(). - Shock pct is percent, not fraction; document in both the module docstring and the config field comment if one is added (do not change config.py). - Construction raises ValueError on invalid parameters; hooks never raise for domain reasons. - Python 3.12-compatible.
